reports.title: Cummins Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results

guidance.heading: 2026 Outlook
section: Based on its current forecast, Cummins expects revenue growth of approximately 10% compared to our prior guidance of 10% to 13%. EBITDA margins are expected to be approximately 18.2%, consistent with our prior guidance range of 18% to 18.5%, and excluding charges related to the sale of the low-pressure fuel cell business in the first quarter.
Cummins plans to continue generating strong operating cash flow and returns for shareholders and is committed to our goal of returning 50% of operating cash flow back to shareholders.

"We have updated our full-year revenue and profitability guidance primarily due to continued weaker than expected pickup truck demand in North America, which impacted our third quarter and is expected to persist through the end of this year,” said Rumsey. “Global power generation and North America heavy duty truck demand remain strong, and we expect fourth quarter revenues to step up from third quarter levels and set a new record."

desk.headline: Revenue up 13% to $9.4bn but short of estimates; record 18.9% EBITDA margin; 2026 sales growth cut to about 10%
results: Sales rose 13% to $9.4bn (North America +15%, international +11%), but missed the $9.9bn analysts expected.
Diluted EPS was $8.25, against $3.86 a year ago when Accelera write-downs cost $1.73; the quarter included $0.54 of one-off tax gains.
EBITDA hit a record 18.9% of sales; Power Systems, driven by data-centre generators, earned a 25.4% margin.
Engine and Components sales rose 20% and 23% as U.S. truck demand recovered; Distribution grew only 4% and its margin fell.
Cash from operations was $1.4bn and $661m went back to shareholders; the quarterly dividend was raised to $2.20 in July.

guidance.summary: Cummins now expects 2026 revenue growth of about 10%, the bottom of its earlier 10–13% range, because of weaker pickup-truck engine demand. The EBITDA margin target of about 18.2% sits inside the earlier 18–18.5% range.

points: Power generation orders beat expectations, with international data-centre orders now matching U.S. orders; power-gen growth outlook held at 15–25%.
About half the revenue shortfall came from weak pickup demand and half from a supplier problem that pushed roughly $200m of Distribution sales into Q4.
North American pickup engine forecast cut to 118,000–122,000 units (from 125,000–140,000) and medium-duty truck output to 125,000–130,000.
Management expects record Q4 revenue, with heavy-duty truck and power-gen demand still strong.
It won its largest battery storage order yet, for a U.S. data centre, and is preparing 2027 engine launches.
call.source: Press release (Exhibit 99) and Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Q4 delivers the promised record revenue as delayed Distribution sales come through.
Pickup engine demand and the North American truck cycle ahead of the 2027 X15 engine launch.
Data-centre power generation orders and capacity.
